project.description: Puzzle game with worlds, levels, progression, shop, and in-app purchases

engine_architecture.issue: Game logic is split between useGame (React layer) and GameEngine (core), leading to an inverted architecture

current_state.useGame: acts as main game engine (state + rules + geometry + validation triggers)
current_state.core_engine: underutilized and not source of truth

problems: game logic lives in UI layer instead of core
hard to test gameplay independently from React
risk of duplicated or inconsistent logic
misleading naming (GameEngine is not actually the engine)

target_architecture.GameEngine: stateful, single source of truth for game state and rules
target_architecture.useGame: thin adapter between UI events and GameEngine

planned_actions: move path state and logic into GameEngine
move intersection and collision rules into core
move star collection logic into core
introduce a stateful GameEngine (start, move, end, reset)

responsibilities: wrap app with providers (ads, gesture handler)
configure system UI (status bar, navigation bar)

state.ready: boolean - indicates if app initialization is complete

tests.purpose: basic routing, smoke tests, and level retrieval validation

GameEngine.role: lightweight helper for segment processing (not a full game engine)
GameEngine.description: Processes a movement segment and updates visited points based on collision detection

behavior: if a point is hit → increment its visit count
if no hit → return visited unchanged

CollisionEngine.description: Provides utility methods to detect interactions between user input (points or segments) and game points (circles)

isPointTouched.description: Checks if a finger position is inside a point radius

detectTouchedPoint.description: Returns the first point touched by the finger
detectTouchedPoint.limitation: returns first match, not necessarily closest

segmentIntersectsCircle.description: Checks if a segment intersects a circle using quadratic equation

detectSegmentHit.description: Returns the first point intersected by a segment
detectSegmentHit.limitation: does not guarantee nearest collision point

limitations: no ordering of collisions (closest vs farthest)
returns first match based on array order
no support for multiple simultaneous collisions
no collision metadata (distance, impact point, t value)

Validator.role: basic completion validator (checks visit counts only)
Validator.description: Validates that each point has been visited the exact required number of times

validate.logic: returns true only if visited count equals required value for every point

rules_checked: each point must be visited exactly point.value times
Validator.architecture_note: This is not a full game validator. It only checks completion and should be extended or replaced by a full GameEngine validation layer.

PathEngine.role: handles player input and path construction
PathEngine.description: Tracks finger movement, builds the path, and updates visited points based on collisions

onFingerStart.description: initializes path and detects first point touch

onFingerMove.description: adds new position and detects collisions with points

current_limitations: can register multiple visits for same point without movement
uses point detection instead of segment detection
PathEngine.architecture_note: This class acts as a partial GameEngine but lacks full rule enforcement and validation.

GraphGenerator.role: generates a grid-based graph structure for levels
GraphGenerator.description: Creates points arranged in a grid with optional jitter and connects them via edges
generation_logic: connects each point to right and bottom neighbors
limitations: no gameplay data (point values all set to 0)
edges are not used by the game engine
GraphGenerator.architecture_note: This generator only creates the spatial structure. Gameplay logic (values, solution paths) must be added by other systems like ValueAssigner or SolverValidator.

LevelGenerator.description: Generates a complete playable level by combining graph creation, solution building, validation, and gameplay assignment
limitations: stars are trivially assigned to solution path
silent error handling in catch block
LevelGenerator.architecture_note: Acts as the central orchestrator of procedural generation. Future improvements include seed-based generation, richer star mechanics, and stronger contracts between modules.

PathBuilder.role: builds a valid traversal path within a graph
PathBuilder.description: Generates a simple path of a given length by performing a random walk on the graph without revisiting nodes
generation_steps: stop when no candidates or target length reached
retry until valid path is found
limitations: purely random (no control over path shape)
can generate trivial or uninteresting paths
high retry rate for longer paths
PathBuilder.design_note: This builder ensures structural validity but not gameplay quality. It should be enhanced or complemented by heuristics or post-processing to produce more interesting puzzles.

SolverValidator.role: validates structural correctness of a generated solution path
SolverValidator.description: Ensures that a generated path respects graph connectivity and visit constraints, without evaluating gameplay rules or puzzle quality
checks: each step moves along a valid edge
each node is visited at most maxVisits times
limitations: does not ensure uniqueness of solution
SolverValidator.design_note: Despite its name, this module does not solve puzzles or validate gameplay correctness. It should be considered a structural validator and may need to be complemented by a real solver for advanced generation.

ValueAssigner.role: derives node values from the generated solution path
ValueAssigner.description: Assigns values to each point based on how many times it is visited in the generated solution, ensuring consistency between generation and validation

steps: count occurrences of each point in the solution path
assign visit count to corresponding points

strengths: no desync between solution and puzzle
ValueAssigner.design_note: This module belongs to generation because it derives puzzle data directly from the known solution. However, it currently acts as a direct projection rather than a transformation, which limits gameplay depth.

Level.description: A level contains a graph of points and optional stars used for objectives or rewards
notes: Level should remain pure and not include progression state
Gameplay rules should not be hardcoded here but derived from constraints or generation

Point.description: Represents a position in the level that can hold gameplay information
notes: value represents gameplay information derived from the solution
value can be hidden (null) to introduce uncertainty
future evolution may replace value with a richer typed structure

Star.description: Represents a reward or constraint element, typically linked to a point in the graph
notes: Stars should be linked to points instead of raw coordinates when tied to gameplay
Can be used for optional objectives or constraints

World.role: groups levels into a progression unit
World.description: Represents a collection of levels forming a world

GetLevels.description: Fetches levels for a given world and enriches them with completion status based on player progression

outputs.LevelWithProgress[]: list of levels with isCompleted flag

flow: merge results to compute isCompleted for each level
rules: isCompleted = true if progress.completedLevels[level.id] > 0
default to false if level not found in progress
edge_cases: no levels returned → empty array
missing progress entry → treated as not completed
undefined completedLevels → should be guarded upstream
test_cases: returns levels with correct isCompleted=true when progress exists
architecture_notes: pure function (no side effects except data fetching)
aggregates multiple repositories into a single view model

CompleteLevel.description: Updates player progression when a level is completed, storing the best score and granting rewards

inputs.levelId: string - identifier of the completed level
inputs.stars: number - stars earned during the run

flow: retrieve current player state from ProgressRepository
read existing stars for the level
compare new stars with existing score
if new score is higher: update completedLevels[levelId]
grant reward based on stars earned
rules: only the best score (max stars) is kept
no update occurs if new stars <= currentStars
reward is granted only when improving score
reward formula: stars * 10 gold

state_mutations.completedLevels: updates levelId entry with new star count

edge_cases: level not yet completed → defaults to 0 stars
same or lower score → no reward, no overwrite
missing completedLevels map → potential crash if not initialized upstream
test_cases: updates level when new stars > existing
does not update when stars <= existing
does not increment gold when not improved
handles new level with no prior progress
architecture_notes: contains business rules for progression and rewards
could be extended with achievements, unlocks, or analytics hooks

playerState.description: Represents the player's progression and currency

rules: first level of a world is always unlocked
a level is unlocked if previous level is completed
a world is unlocked if previous world is fully completed
stars overwrite only if higher than previous
gold reward = stars * 10

ads.overview: AdMob integration with safe initialization, rate limiting, and environment-based ad units

responsibilities: initialize AdMob SDK safely (with timeout fallback)
provide canLoadAd() guard to prevent spam requests
rules: ads cannot load before SDK initialization
minimum delay between loads: 30s
initialization is executed only once (singleton)

responsibilities: display banner ads based on placement
rules: do not render if adMode = no_ads
do not load if canLoadAd() returns false
refresh controlled via refreshKey (not setInterval)
fallback placeholder shown before first load
ad must be created after mount (avoid native crash)
reload automatically after closing
show only if loaded

responsibilities: store all ad unit IDs (banner + interstitial)
switch between test and production IDs
rules: test ads used in dev or unsafe environments
production requires valid IDs (no 'XXX')
platform-specific mapping (iOS/Android)

architecture_notes: fully isolated from gameplay and domain logic
designed to avoid crashes, spam, and policy violations
tech_debt: adMode not yet connected to purchase system (remove_ads)
interstitial placement logic still manual (not tied to gameplay events)
no centralized ad manager (logic split across hooks/components)

iap.overview: RevenueCat-based in-app purchase system with paywall UI and entitlement management

responsibilities: normalize paywall outcome into boolean success/failure

integration_points: connected to AdProvider via adMode = no_ads
should update PlayerState or global state after purchase
tech_debt: no synchronization with PlayerState (ads still enabled unless manually handled)
no caching of purchase state (calls RevenueCat each time)
no retry/backoff strategy on network failure
package selection is naive (always first available)
no support for multiple products (only no_ads)

db.description: Lightweight async wrapper around expo-sqlite with singleton connection
responsibilities: initialize SQLite database lazily (on first use)

internal.getDb: opens database 'game.db' once and reuses it

rules: database connection must not be recreated multiple times
all queries must go through this adapter
parameters must be passed separately (prevent SQL injection)
error_handling: no internal try/catch → errors propagate to caller
architecture_notes: acts as a gateway between app and SQLite
easily replaceable (e.g., with Realm or async storage)
edge_cases: concurrent calls during first initialization (potential race condition)
database corruption not handled
no transaction helper (multi-query atomicity missing)
tech_debt: no transaction support (BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK wrapper missing)
no migration/version enforcement at this level

initDatabase.description: Bootstraps database schema and applies versioned migrations
responsibilities: create core tables if they do not exist
track database version via meta table
ensure schema consistency at app startup
rules: must be called once at app startup (root layout)
must run before any repository access
db_version must always reflect latest applied migration
error_handling: no internal try/catch → errors bubble to app initializer
caller logs 'Init error' (as defined in root layout)
architecture_notes: simple manual migration system (no external ORM)
edge_cases: no transaction wrapping → partial migration risk if crash occurs
concurrent init calls could duplicate work (rare but possible)
string-based version storage requires parsing (Number(value))
tech_debt: db.get used without await causing TypeScript error (TS2339) and runtime bug where currentVersion is always 0
recommended_improvements: wrap migrations in a transaction (BEGIN / COMMIT)
consider splitting progress into structured tables if querying is needed

migrations.description: Versioned migration system using _migrations table to track applied schema changes
flow: apply each migration conditionally (if currentVersion < N)
insert version after each successful migration

queries: CREATE TABLE progress (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, data TEXT NOT NULL)

v2.description: reserved for future changes (example: add updatedAt column)

rules: must be executed at app startup
must be awaited (async execution)
each migration must be idempotent
version must be inserted only after success
error_handling: no internal try/catch → errors bubble up
should be wrapped in transaction for safety
architecture_notes: keeps infrastructure independent from business logic
edge_cases: missing await can cause repeated migrations
no transaction → partial migration risk
concurrent execution could duplicate inserts
no rollback mechanism

levelRepository.description: Provides access to worlds and levels loaded from static JSON data
responsibilities: expose read-only access to worlds and levels
abstract data source from domain logic
edge_cases: returns null if world or level not found
getNextLevel returns null if last level
no validation of duplicated IDs
architecture_notes: can be replaced by remote API without impacting domain

progressRepository.description: Handles persistence of player progression state using SQLite
responsibilities: initialize default state if none exists
error_handling: creates default state if no row exists
resets to default if JSON is corrupted
edge_cases: JSON corruption handled with full reset
no partial recovery of data
single save key limits multi-profile support
tech_debt: no schema validation for stored JSON
no migration strategy for PlayerState evolution
full overwrite on save (no partial updates)
architecture_notes: acts as persistence gateway for progression
could evolve into event-based or normalized storage
currently optimized for simplicity over scalability

levelLoader.description: Loads and maps level data from local JSON files into domain models
responsibilities: map JSON structure to domain models (World, Level)
normalize property names between data and domain
limitations: only loads world1.json (no multi-world support yet)
uses 'any' type for level mapping (unsafe typing)
edge_cases: invalid JSON structure can crash mapping
missing fields are not validated
no fallback if data is malformed
tech_debt: mixes static data with gameplay state (isCompleted, isAvailable)
no separation between content and progression
recommended_improvements: support multiple world files (world1, world2, world3)
remove gameplay state from loader (move to ProgressionService)
allow async loading for future remote support
architecture_notes: acts as anti-corruption layer between raw data and domain
prepares future migration to remote data source
currently tightly coupled to file structure

progressLoader.description: Loads and maps player progression data from SQLite into domain models
progressLoader.output: Player progression state (completed levels, unlocked levels, etc.)
responsibilities: map database rows to domain state
provide default state if no data exists
edge_cases: no existing data (first launch)
corrupted or partial data
schema mismatch after update
tech_debt: no migration handling at this level
architecture_notes: complements LevelLoader by providing dynamic player state
should be merged with domain via ProgressionService
acts as data source, not business logic holder
